summary: Sri Anirvan (1896–1978) was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He studied at the Sanskrit College and University (~1914–1916), the University of Calcutta (~1916–1918), and the University of Dhaka.

Sri Aurobindo (1872–1950) worked in philosophy, Indology, and religious studies. He studied at St Paul's School and King's College, Cambridge, and under Robert Mason Towers, Dinendra Kumar Ray, and Vishnu Bhaskar Lele. He held a post at Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda (~1893–1906).

Srikanth Kaul was a scholar in Indology and history/archaeology. In 1967, he was attested as a professor at the Research and Archaeological Department, Jammu and Kashmir, and held a post at Government Degree College, Sopore.

Srilata Raman is a scholar in Indology and religious studies. She served as a Lecturer in Sanskrit at Heidelberg University (attested 2005) and has held posts as Assistant Professor (attested 2008) and Associate Professor of Hinduism (attested 2020–2024) at the University of Toronto.

Srimanta Bhadra is a scholar in Indology, philosophy, and linguistics. He earned a Ph.D. from Ramakrishna Mission Vivekananda Educational and Research Institute by 2021 and served as an Assistant Professor at Raja Narendra Lal Khan Women's College in 2017.

Srinivas H. Ritti (1928–2021) worked in Indology and history/archaeology. He served as an Epigraphical Assistant at the Archaeological Survey of India (attested 1964) and Government Epigraphist for India (attested 1965), and as Professor at Karnatak University (attested 1975).

Srinivasa Ayya Srinivasan (1932–2019) was an Indology scholar who earned his Dr. phil. at the University of Hamburg (~1962–1967). He served as Privatdozent für Indologie at the University of Hamburg from 1973 to 1997.

Srinivasa Kumar N Acharya is an Indology and philosophy scholar. He studied at Poornaprajna Vidyapeetha (MA Vidvat-uttama Navya-nyaya) and became an Assistant Professor at Manipal Academy of Higher Education in 2011.

Sriram Krishnan works in computational linguistics and Indology. He has held posts at Central Sanskrit University, the International Institute of Information Technology, Hyderabad, and the University of Hyderabad.

Sriram Subramanian works in Indology and computational fields. He studied at Pondicherry Engineering College, the University of Cincinnati, Hindu University of America, and MIT Group of Institutions. In 2022, he was a Principal Software Engineer at Microsoft.

Srisa Chandra Vasu (1861–1918) was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He earned a BA at Government College University, Lahore (~1877–1881), founded the Panini Office in 1891, was a Vakil at Allahabad High Court (attested 1891), and was a Fellow at the University of Allahabad.

Stacey Boulter is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. She studied at Dalhousie University (BA 2016–2025) and McMaster University (MA 2025), where she served as a Teaching Assistant in 2025.

Stacey Van Vleet works in Tibetology, history/archaeology, and sinology. She studied under Carole McGranahan and Tashi Tsering Josayma, earned an M.A. at the University of Colorado Boulder, and completed a Ph.D. and held a post at Columbia University.

Stamford Raffles (1781–1826) worked in history/archaeology and linguistics. He held posts with the East India Company, served as Chief Secretary of Prince of Wales Island (1807) and Governor of Java (~1811–1816), and founded the Zoological Society of London.

Stanford E. Lehmberg (1931–2012) was a history/archaeology scholar. He earned his PhD at the University of Cambridge under Christopher Morris (~1954–1956) and was an emeritus professor at the University of Minnesota Twin Cities (~1999–2012).
Stanislao Gatti (1820–1870) was a scholar in philosophy and Indology. He studied at the University of Naples Federico II, where he later held a post from ~1861 to 1870.

Stanislas Guyard (1846–1884) worked in Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He served as Répétiteur and Directeur d’études at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (1868) and became Professor of Arabic at the Collège de France (1884).

Stanislas Julien (1797–1873) was a scholar of sinology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied under Jean-Pierre Abel-Rémusat at the Collège de France, where he later held the Chair of Chinese (1832–1873), and taught at the Institut national des langues et civilisations orientales.

Stanislav Grof (born 1931) studied at Charles University (~1950–1956). His career includes positions at Kosmonosy, Psychiatrické centrum Praha, Johns Hopkins University, Maryland Psychiatric Research Center, Esalen Institute (1973–1987), and California Institute of Integral Studies (1994–2015).
Stanislav Mudra (born 1910) was an Indology scholar. He studied at Charles University, completing his Ph.D. at the Faculty of Arts under the supervision of Otakar Pertold.
